text: River Cree Casino is great!  Nice atmosphere!  I'm also a huge fan of Sage, the restaurant.  The steak and ceaser salad is yummy!
The casino is smoky like most casinos. The hotel is smoke free and was not bad, smoky smell wise, and was clean. I had a restful night sleep and would definitely stay again. The price was reasonable.

Not a gambler, but found myself here with friends. Was it entertaining? I'd have to say yes, but maybe because I lost 50$ instead of 200$. There was a dangerous thrill in going down 200$ early and bringing yourself back to a respectable loss. I understand the concept of a gambling addiction now as I felt definite heart palpitations. Losing 200$ and I'd might never ever come back.

It's a huge casino and people watching alone here would be fun particularly if you were doing a sociology or psychology thesis! Lots of characters from different shapes, sizes and ages. 

It's far out west and I wouldn't necessarily say it's worth it to travel that far for a night out. However, if you are bored and are looking for something different you would be entertained here!
River Cree does not return emails and phone calls. Guest Services is not very knowlegeable

Over the years, I have experienced "The Venue", banquets, and "The Kitchen" restaurant. The River Cree Resort & Casino overall is a pretty cool facility with several restaurants, a casino, a hotel, ice rinks, a venue for concerts/shows, and banquet facilities.  While the location is kind of random (except not really random as it was purposely placed on reserve land), it is very close to West Edmonton Mall. So I can see out of town people being attracted to the River Cree for a weekend stay.

I ate at the Kitchen many, many times over the years, but not recently. It was average for a buffet... 3 stars. If you have the River Cree players card, you get a discount. 

I went to a concert at "The Venue", which was poorly set up when I went (perhaps it's changed). What I remember is it was winter, and we checked our coats, headed over the venue, and had to walk OUTSIDE to get to it. So odd.

I've booked the banquet facilities a couple of times and I will say the banquet manager was always very easy to deal with. Most people liked the food. However, one year for our corporate event (awards), there was a hopping party (maybe a wedding) in the banquet hall we shared a wall with, and the music and bass was so loud it was like we weren't even in separate rooms. 

Overall, this is an average facility... probably worth checking out if it peaks your interest.
Gambling first.What did ya expect.Getting a little dated.Food is ok.Drinking ok.Good retro live acts.

Food is pretty good and a good value. But the cigarette smoke is unbearable.

Buffet had good selection and was prepared well.

I'm not much of a gambler but I have to Vegas.  I've also been to a few casinos in Edmonton and are nothing like the glitz and glam of Sin City.  But River Cree is, by far, the closest thing to a Vegas-style Casino that you will find in Edmonton and probably Alberta.  

First of all, there is smoking allowed in this Casino.  Half of the Casino floor is smoking and half is non-smoking.  

This place is always packed.  I've been to the Casino for a few events and one birthday party and every time it is jam-packed with gamblers and party-goers.  

The drinks are expensive here, which makes it even more Vegas-like.  The food is pretty good too.  There are a few different venues for people who don't gamble.  They have clubs, restaurants, bars, and special events going on all the time.  

It's a pretty happening place so if you're tired of Edmonton night life, check out River Cree for something new and exciting!

Great time, super clean plus you can smoke inside!! 
Crab was great at the buffet restaurant!

Located in the deep west end of Edmonton, there are more convenient and friendlier casinos to lose your money in. 

The security staff working Friday nights look like they're having an enema.  The management make it clear that ANY problem you're having is yours.  The fact that smoking is allowed detracts from any charms this place may have. 

Parking is terrible and the lack of traffic controls exiting after a show are horrendous and scary.  If you have to attend a show here, bring lots of patience.

We recently had gone to River Cree for a show. The entertainment they bring in is always pretty good. We had gone to a show before there and did not have an issue.
This time supper was included. YUCK YUCK YUCK. They had a potato salad,Coleslaw and some other salad they all tasted exactly the same. And lets just say it was not a good taste it all tasted like mayo. If we ever attend a show at the casino again we will definetly make sure we eat before we go.

The River Cree Resort is probably the closest you can get to a Vegas style get away without leaving the city. 

The casino is really nice looking, very classy and has over 30 table games and tons of slot machines. The hotel is equally as nice and kept in top shape. The resort also has two NHL size ice rinks where people can go for pick up games or watch the Oilers practice every now and then. They also have a few different restaurants and lounges to choose from that all offer good food and service. The resort also hosts concerts, comedy acts and more.. Conan O'Brien is coming next week.

It is really far North so it is out of the way for most locals but it is definitely a great place to visit if you are coming for vacation.

Awesome facility here with excellent food and service ! I had the buffet here and it was great . Place is clean and employees security are all friendly and happy and look like they enjoy their jobs . Prices are fair and lots of tables and games here . I would give 5 stars immediately but I hate smoking and cigarettes are permitted here in places.

Went to ABBA, the show was great but the food  prior was awful. Wings and pay cash up front. After the show you can use your drink tickets and I got a drink and went to the bathroom and when I went to go back to my husband and drink security said the bar was too full and I couldn't go in that area. Wow, how many people bought and drink headed to the washroom and were then denied access to the drink they just bought. I was not impressed. My husband had to come out of the bar area and we list our table.

Big disappointment. My husband and I decided to stop in for a couple of drinks on the way home after running some errands. We sat on the smoke-FILLED non-smoking side and watched 3 waitresses tend to other patrons without acknowledging us. The floor manager also walked by 4 times without acknowledgment. After 20 minutes of waiting, we decided to leave. We will go the extra 5 minutes to surrounding pubs/restaurants before returning to the River Cree. So disappointing as we were excited to stop in and enjoy the establishment.

Spent the night at the Marriot and it was a pleasant stay. The room was a standard hotel room and very clean and quiet and the rate was good. 
I was surprised by the amount of smoke in the Casino. After being in the Casino for an hour I stunk of smoke and my eyes were so dry. 
We had dinner at the Sage restaurant and was disappointed.  Calamari was cold and the chowder was salty both lacked the luster. It defiantly was not worth what we paid.

This a nicer casino in Alberta. It is relatively new so it doesn't have the stale look or smell. The location is a bit of a drive but its worthwhile for sure. There a well managed Marriott as hotel and it seems to be gaining  steam with an event almost every weekend. The management likes to push the entertainment venue well and I loved when they had the tribute band marathon  while I was there. You get discounts of almost all the places in the resort including Starbucks!!!
The buffet is one of the decent one's and while there are not many dishes they are quite diverse.There is a good area for non smokers one doesn't stink afterwards.  They have a decent set of concerts here regularly. Plenty of parking as well. The best casino in Alberta if not Canada IMO.
Fun place to go. One of the better casinos in town. Get a players card if you want to get food perks. The kitchen buffet is very good and always fresh.

I came to the city to play a little poker at the River Cree. It was definitely an enjoyable atmosphere to play in.

Annually, I play in poker rooms all over Vegas, unlike many poker rooms this place felt new & fresh. Usually when the poker room is a cordoned off space on the main floor, the slot machines are overwhelmingly loud to the point that you can't hear yourself think. That wasn't the case here at all. The music played in the background but wasn't overpowering. 

The players were all very friendly. It was like playing in a large home game, as everyone was catching up with everyone else.

The pit boss & dealers were also very friendly & very professional. The desk had a digital photo frame that slowly displayed pertinent information for upcoming tournaments & scheduled events. Compared to many things I've seen, I thought it was a classy presentation.

I will definitely return. :) In fact, I can't wait! :D

Pluses: Circular casino, very logically arranged. Good deals on food, and what food we had was very enjoyable. The First Nations security staff were pleasant, professional and friendly.

On the plus or minus side, depending: If you are in the smoker minority, you'll love this place; smoking is allowed, and the whole place reeks. Trust me, you won't even need to light up in order to have your clothes smelling like a forest fire by the time you leave. Um, yum, I guess?

Minuses: We made the mistake of stopping by the bar for their breakfast special. The bartender would only approach the far end when someone grabbed another staff member to get his attention. Once fed (the food was great), it was nearly impossible to pay. We watched in fascination as several people sat down, waited, grew impatient, and finally left in disgust, while this individual steadfastly refused to as much as return a glance, much less acknowledge the growing sea of waving arms. It was obvious that some sort of work-to-rule protest was going on, with the public the victims, though the staff were far from overworked.

In short, while the casino has its high points, our overall impression was not good. It seems like a hanger-on from the roaring days of the oil boom, when businesses could get away with third-rate service.

This is your typical Pub though very reasonably priced if you have the casino card (usually means a main for 10$). I like this place for UFC events as they have a huge projection screen and plenty of TV screens. The best part is there is no cover and beer is reasonably priced not much of a selection though as mostly local brews. They had the steak and fries special when I tried it and the steak was OK but for the price I paid it was a good value. The Service is decent and the staff is friendly.

I love food and this place just didn't do it.  You know in vegas the food is amazing.  yes I get it this isn't vegas.  Restaurant is nice enough but everything is just OK... and by O.K. I mean its like eating a Smitty's buffet... maybe a touch better.  Yes, Yes what about the special nights with seafood and ribs buffet... again its just ok.  Quality over quantity.  If you like to just fill up, then this is the place for you.  The desserts are mass produced and there is 1 or 2 that are good to go back for seconds.

We were just to the Venue to watch a PPV boxing match...they had a buffet...it was the worst buffet I have ever been to...hard cold hamburgers...cold hard fries...dry hard chicken wings...this is twice we have had terrible food at this venue...the other was NYE at the Sage...$350. And one of the worst meals I have ever had.

NOT Handicap Friendly. I use a walker and my wife uses a cane. We were forced to walk through the casino to get access to the venue. The handicap seating was just as narrow as the rest of the seating with no area to store walkers. The seating spaces were too narrow for wheel chairs. We asked 5 security and other staff if there was a shorter way to leave the venue before we found someone who knew a short cut. Unfortunately she was located at the casino entrance. Handicapped people using canes/walkers can enter through the Arena Entrance. It is not marked as a Handicapped Venue Entrance. The arena door is unlocked in March. You should check if it is unlocked if you are attending in the summer.

The staff in the casino are very nice and quite helpful. I found the restaurants overpriced except for the taproom. There's a lot going on at the River Cree so if you enjoy games of chance with the many venues that they bring in... Do you like it here X

So. I was north....waaaaay up north in Edmonton.  I didn't go to "you know where", but I did go to the River Cree Casino.  This is where I've heard stories of the HUGE Enoch Pow Wow in August.  So, I had to go to this casino to just check it out.

I'm not a gambler, but a friend and I went here for lunch.  So, we took a tour of the casino.  It's a nice casino, and it is obviously doing brisk business.  It was pretty happening and packed.  

The casino is fairly Las Vegas-ish, but it was also Canadian.  What makes it Canadian, you ask??

HOCKEY RINK.

They have a hockey rink right there in the freakin' casino!  There was a pick up game going on, and hockey was definitely being played!  There is a restaurant bar adjacent to the rink so one can peer through the window and see people getting body checked as they eat their shrimp scampi.

"The Venue" at River Cree brings in some great acts, and I'm a sucker for comedy shows... so sadly, I'll be back.  Aside from the shows though, it is really not a great experience.

I will say that the security staff are incredibly friendly.  Despite the fact that they were turning us away at the door because my friend didn't realize she couldn't use her expired ID to get in.  The staff were polite and we jumped back in my car to run home to grab her passport.  

I had purchased tickets to the Chris D'Elia show on February 6th for her birthday and we had planned on eating there before the show.

By the time we drove home and back, it was 7:30 (show starts at 9).  I figured it would be tight, but didn't imagine that we wouldn't be able to get a seat for dinner anywhere.  I had really wanted to go to Sage, but when we walked by, they were clearly packed and we chose to just keep walking.  We got to Tap 25. They had a 40 minute wait time for a table.  That wouldn't be enough time so we scurried over to the buffet.  No luck there - the wait was about 25 minutes (it was almost 7:50 by this point because we had to wait in line at Tap 25 to find out there was a 40 minute wait).

Screw it.  We noticed a "grab and go" place as we were running around, so we just grabbed some hot dogs and then headed into the venue to find our seats.

The "new" venue is not much better than the old one.  You follow the signs in the casino to get there, and end up walking down a loooong hallway, passed their ice rink and then OUTSIDE to get to the venue.  Again, I have to commend the security staff for doing a good job of keeping every one orderly.  When Chris D'Elia came on stage, one of the first things he said was that it looked and felt like he was performing in an airplane hangar.

Drinks were a bit of a mess - you had to line up to buy drink tickets, and then line up again to get your drink.  they were mixed well, but nowhere NEAR worth $9.00 a piece.  That was ridiculous.

 The show was awesome... but for the price, i expected to be sitting on something better than a folding chair.  And there were times when I found the sound to be quite piercing.

The real nightmare came at the end of the show.  WHEN THERE WAS ONLY ONE EXIT FOR 2100 PEOPLE!  Are you kidding me?  There were several other doors around the outside of the venue, that were NOT indicated as emergency exits only, but when people tried to use them, they ended up being turned around to come back in and wait in line with the rest of us.

Also, if you have to go to the restroom during the show, you have to go back outside and then into the rink area.

Oh - and another strange thing.  As you walk passed the rink, there is a concession stand.  MANY people assumed that that was the concession stand for the venue and stopped to get coffee or pizza, only to find out at the door that they couldn't bring it in with them.  The concession staff should have been advising people of that - or at least put up a sign or something.

My Yelp resolution for 2016 was to stop rambling so much in interviews and just get to the point, but clearly that didn't work so well.  So....

TL:DR - You will absolutely enjoy your show. But the rest of it will be a nightmare.

I went to the buffet today for lunch and was very disappointed with management & how they handled the situation. I noticed my jello was moldy and told the manager on. He said he was sorry and walked away. Never asked if he could get me anything or do anything about it.

The rooms here are quite large and they have ample room for large banquets, dinners and even large shows/concerts.  The staff we encountered were friendly enough.  Nothing really stands out except their Sunday brunch was excellent.  They had lots of seafood and shrimp cocktails.  The food was elaborately presented and everything was great.  I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

Very impressive. Clean with lots of slot machines and blackjack tables. We came after New Years so Christmas decorations still up which looked amazing. Tipi decorations outside. Lots of parking available. Washrooms very clean and the security staffs were very friendly

We stayed here for the Foreigner concert. Great concert! Fabulous staff that work at the hotel, casino and event. The beds are very comfortable! Love that they have a Starbucks and microwave on the room. The bathroom is functional but the tub is super small as it's a standard tub. Clean and suitable for our stay.

I guess it's nice?
It has all the bells and whistles.  
Casinos are NOT my thing.  I usually just walk through to get to where I'm going.  This one is least maze-like than many.  
We attended a show on a busy Friday night.  The venue is pretty good.  Traffic moves quickly. There are 2 bars slinging $8.00 drinks.
The washrooms are nice.
After the show, we stopped for a drink at one of the few restaurants.  We waited at the bar until we were paged for our table. They had Granville Island IPA on tap!
 We ordered nachos.  They were horrible. We left. 
I hate the smell of cigarettes. It's thick with smoke in the casino.  Gross.  I probably won't go back.

One of my favourite bites when I'm in town.  A decade ago when table wait times were  1-2hr and my regular order out was pizza or anything in the pantry I was happy to discover this casino served the top grade meat, the top grade desserts and the top grade everything.  Main advise get in early for the restaurant else your in a line up.

When you join their membership you get free money primarily based on your demographic to use in the buffet or in the casino.

I dropped the rating a star because they had a privacy breach and all I received was a notice by mail-thrilling.  Now someone else knows my home address my name and age... :/

The lousy security on customer data is a bit concerning.

I've never actually been to the casino part of the river cree, anytime I come here,  it's for dinner. The restaurant is huge, it's great that they have lots of tables, but I've found that when it's a busy night, the tables feel a little too close together, especially when there's lots of people always getting up to go for food. The Buffett usually has lots of great choices and is maintained well, the dessert selection is my personal favourite! I do enjoy coming here for dinner, but it is a little on the pricey side so I usually don't order drinks when I come here. Overall, the dining area is quite nice and well kept. From what I've seen of the casino, it looks huge! But again, I can't review that part as I've never been inside it, I'm not much of a gambler anyway.

This is a SMOKING facility, with very poor ventilation.

If you have allergies, pulmonary challenges or are otherwise sensitive to burned tobacco, you should avoid this place.

I won't be back.

Since hubby is away on business, I thought I'd check out the casino and grab a bite to eat while I was there. 

The casino looks very nice and has a good mix of older and new fancy slots. I wandered around, sat for a bit and spent a few dollars. I was stunned that see that people were smoking in here! All I can say is "Holy Toledo" the smell of cigarette smoke in here is ridiculous!!! 

My eyes began burning and I actually felt nauseous just sitting there! I never did end up getting anything to eat as I really felt unwell after a short time there. 

The 2 stars are for the many staff members there who seemed very friendly and helpful. I will not be back.

Love this casino! Wide variety of games and a great place to see top notch entertainment. Hotel is clean, comfortable and upscale. There is also no shortage of restaurants to choose from regardless of what you may be in the mood for. Great spot!

On New Year's Eve I took my wife and son to see a show. We were minding our own business, when we started getting hassled by an extremely drunk and belligerent guy. I called over a Filipino security guard, who is completely inapt, and failed to do anything about it successfully in my mind, I told him to keep an eye on him, but then I on this gentleman because we would have more problems with them that night. He should've been removed from the facility immediately.
Sure enough about 20 minutes later he came back over again being extremely drunk and belligerent hassling me and my wife, I stood up grabbed him and pushed him aside and told him to stop bothering us,Finally the chief of security got involved again I explained what was going on we just came here for a nice evening to relax I asked that he be removed he was not, she said she keep an eye on them so for the rest of the evening he was glaring at us across the table. It completely ruined a nice evening for us I really felt at the River Cree could've done more to assist us, either remove that guy or put us at a different table at the very least, I was very disappointed in the way it was handled
One of the best Casinos in Edmonton only place that allows smoking indoors in 2018 however if your a non smoker like me you cant even smell it so its not a bother.

Edmonton and area is becoming the casino capital of the country.  The River Cree gets as close as it can to the resorts in Vegas with the different types of restaurants, The Kitchen Buffet offers a different type of buffet nightly, Tap 25 is where you can catch a hockey game on one of the big screens while enjoying pub type food, and Sage if you are looking for a sophisticated dining experience.  I have eaten at the buffet and was a little disappointed with the food options but the strawberry shortcake was good! Tap 25 gets busy, especially on concert nights so come early before 6PM to get a table.  The food is decent and good fries too.  I highly recommend getting a Players card as they have a food special for Tap 25 which gets you a decent meal for $10-$11.

Even if you aren't a big gambler, River Cree has a great marketing plan to get people into the door.  They offer draws on certain days with prizes that include cash, cars, and other enticing prizes.  The draws are held hourly so it's easy for people to stay all evening waiting for their name to be drawn and in between spend money on gambling, eating, and drinking.  If you go there more frequent, you usually have a greater chance of winning with more ballots in the draw drum.

The casino offers a variety of tables with different limits.  There's also many slot machines including a section for smokers.  It can get busy on the weekends so the game you want to play might be taken but I'm sure you can find another.  In Tap 25 they also have off track horse racing on the TVs so lots of way to gamble here.

Since the place is a circle, lots of washrooms around here and clean too.  They also have them in the adjoining hotel and clean and no waiting in line here.

The Venue offers a place to watch bands, see comedians, and other entertainment.  My review of it will be separate from this one.  

If you are a regular at this casino, get to know the hosts.  They can provide comps when you befriend them and if they recognize you.  Who doesn't like a free meal or show? 

Not a place that everyone will enjoy but not bad if you want to catch a game while you grab a beer, try your luck at cards, want to enjoy a good meal, or catch a show.

Really amazing buffet! I went to the dinner one that starts at 5pm and by the time they opened there was a huge line to get in. It's a very large dining area and by far the best buffet choices of any competing establishment! Decent pricing and kind staff. Very much a win.

Hotel and Casino plus excellent places to eat at. Security staff is awesome. Staff is great and cleaning protocol top notch. Recommended place for a weekend, not to spend your money at the casino all weekend.

On my 3 week Alberta Poker Tour.

First stop here and I need a card to sign up for the tourney.  Supervisor gets a guy to go get me one and I meet him at the cash cage.  That is first class service.

One of the best run poker tourneys I have ever been in.  Easily the best so far in Alberta.  I love that they give you a personalized name slip when they break tables.

UFC fight on and the whole casino is tuned in.  Dealers, servers and players were all nice.

Cashed in both tournies as I came back another night.  This would be my go to place if I lived here.

We came her once with a bunch of friends a few years ago.  We came for supper at the restaurant but also wandered around the casino a bit and played a few games.

I'm not really into gambling so the casino wasn't my thing and I can't really give an in-depth review to the gaming side of things.  The venue itself is pretty nice and a great facility.  The one huge downside for me though is the smoking and poor ventilation. Anyone with allergies or lung issues is not going to like it here. It is smokey throughout and it could use much more or better ventilation. We ate at the great restaurant there which had great food but the smoke that is present throughout the facility totally ruins it for me.

This is one of Edmonton's larger casinos located west of the Henday just off of the Whitemud freeway.  Unless you drive or take a taxi, it may be difficult to get here.  I have seen the occasional airport taxi.  It is a Las Vegas style place offering a Player's Club card, weekly promotion draws, a centre bar, a concert venue and three restaurants.  The hotel is beautiful and has a few banquet rooms, the lobby is large with couches and chairs and even plug-ins for your laptop.

Many functions are held here, the banquets rooms can accommodate company meetings, parties and weddings and even musical concerts.  The food is usually located in the hallway which does make it a bit awkward for casino patrons walking by.

The Kitchen restaurant offers a nightly buffet.  The selection isn't as large as one would expect and the food just tastes okay.  There are different types of meat such as prime rib, bbq ribs, and seafood depending on the night.  Kids are welcome here as it is located just outside the casino entrance.

Tap 25 is the sports bar and serves food you would typically find in a pub.  The wings are good and I really enjoy the beef dip.  They also have a prime rib special for $9.99 from Sunday to Thursday, excellent deal as it comes with Yorkshire pudding and veggies.  I notice that they have a large staff turnover and service is not always great.  There is off track betting for horse racing in several racetracks located in Canada and the US.

Sage is the more special dining restaurant offering a steak and lobster option and is only open in the evenings.

This is the only casino that has a smoking section.  It can be overpowering especially on the weekend.  If smoke really bothers you, your experience will be less enjoyable.  They only offer $5 blackjack before 7 p.m. in the non-smoking section and never in the smoking section.  Most of the dealers and pit bosses are friendly.

Parking can get really crazy on busy nights when there's a concert or say New Year's Eve.  A new concert venue has been added to replace the old one but I haven't been there yet.  The old one wasn't great as there was one way in and out and just didn't have that "concert" feel.

Recently they started offering free shuttle service to Rexall Place on Oiler game nights.  You need to collect your wrist band from the Player's Club and arrive 2 hours before game time.  The school bus will take you there and back.

This is a fun place to come to with friends, a date or just hang out to eat and try to win money!

Just had our reservation at The Kitchen at the River Cree and it was amazing. This was our second visit to this restaurant, and let me tell you folks, it's worth every penny. Very happy with the amazing service as well, the food was spot on. Both my wife and I enjoyed the steak, cooked to a perfect medium rare, and the desserts were delicious. Only thing I'd say, is, the lobster want perfect, little over cooked, but still tasty. We will be back again. Thanks for having us!!

Very poor neighbours.

They plan outdoor events for 11pm on Sundays, with the ruckus being audible over a kilometre away despite pouring rain.

I can't imagine how loud this would have been on-site.

Being outside of Edmonton, they don't have to abide by the City's noise bylaw.

Avoid if you care about your fellow Edmontonians!

I've been here for their Friday crab buffet for about 5 years now. It has been a nice experience overall. Some of the things that stood out were the clam chowder, mussels, chicken, shrimps, beef, vegetables, various desserts (cakes and fruits), the free drink, and the snow crab legs for a reasonable price. However, they have increased their prices recently to $48+ per person. After comparing their new items (i.e. baked salmon, clams, etc.) with the higher buffet price and the lesser quality crab legs, it's harder to justify paying that much for the AYCE

I've been going to river cree now for the past few years.  Primarily to play craps...mostly 4-5 days a week.  Last week they raised their craps table from 5.00 to 10.00.  They didn't bother to give me a heads up or any sort of warning.  I just went one day and was told it was raised.  Now, most of us "regulars " eventually play a 10.00 game but we like to start with a 5.00 game.  Now our option has been taken away.  Not likely going back there again.  Will be going to casino on Argyl road.

Zero stars, stay far, far away. 

I had planned on stopping in here today (March 12 @ 11:15 am).

The parking lot was very full so I was forced to park very far away. I took ONE step out of my truck and fell flat on my a$$, cracking my elbow on the way down. The lot is a huge sheet of pebbly ice covered with a thin layer of snow.
The casino has neglected to clear/salt/sand over half of this parking lot. 

I immediately went to the rewards desk to report it to someone, but there was only one person on staff as well as a line up. I walked back to the entrance and approached 2 security guards to let them know. They just looked at each other and said nothing. Neither asked if I was ok, or if I was injured. I said "that's it? It's fine?" One guy said "Oh, ok, we'll let them know."

The lack of care and concern for my health following an accident on their property is appalling. 

I left immediately as my back & elbow are hurting and I have a headache. 

Disgraceful treatment of customers here. I will never return.

Very impressive. Clean with lots of slot machines and blackjack tables. We came after New Years so Christmas decorations still up which looked amazing. Tipi decorations outside. Lots of parking available. Most of the machines were occupied.
Lots of Washrooms available and very clean the security staffs were very friendly

Came here for my birthday and Jann Arden was playing.  I had read a previous review of this venue so I was prepared to not get into any of the restaurants and have to grab a hot dog.  That was a bummer but not a big deal.  

We played a few slot machines and had the best service from 2 lovely servers.  And our drinks we great.  We didn't have anything fancy just vodka and soda, but they were great!

We didn't make it rich (money wise) but had a really good time in the casino and for Jann's show.  The audio did seem off a few times, but it didn't spoil the show.  I was happy with the seating, it was arranged really well and the chairs were comfy.  I'd come back here again for a show.  

Only down fall is leaving the venue.  It was a standstill.  No one knew where to go or how to get out.

Went to their new patio tonight and the service was amazing and the food was even better and the prices were very reasonable! Our server, Christina, was so on top of it the whole night and took great care of us. The manager, Dean is also phenomenal and made sure every was well taken care of too. Highly recommend this patio for anyone looking for a nice dinner! Great vibe.

I'm just a girl... literally only reviewing the craps table LOL. This is one of the only places in Edmonton to play craps. I am trying to teach myself how to play so this is my go-to. I literally don't do anything else here but try to teach myself to play craps. 

So basically, my experience here has been great because the dealers, pit bosses, and stickmen (or women), have been SO nice and helpful while I've been learning to play. Even though it is super fun, I don't find craps to be easy to pick up, like at all. Throughout my game they're always helping me understand the rules and bets better. I often have a lot of questions and they're very good at answering those questions for me. The first time I played it was confusing asf. Now it is not too bad.

I am very thankful for all the free (I tip them of course) walk-throughs on how to play. It is straight up like having buddies that let you know what to do! I know they need to bring over two to three staff members to get this game going, and working the game seems extremely difficult. I have no clue how they keep track of everything going on, but they do it, and still find time to coach me. Lovely people!

Had a great breakfast here with some coworkers. The staff were excellent, great service for our large group. The $3.99 breakfast was great, food arrived hot and the portions were excellent for the price. Definitely going to visit again.

The midweek $3.99 breakfast special was definitely worth it. There was a good selection, generous portions and specials orders were handled well. The reuben was nice because not everyone likes breakfast. Fyi, even though the menu says the reuban has mustard, it actually came with 1000 island dressing. The hash browns were not bad and not great either. I would definitely eat there again.

No one can beat the $3.99 breakfast!!!
Cousin & i decided to have a mothers day brunch here.. i am a first timer & she's a regular customer..
No complaints on service & foodies..
Definitely coming back

Stopped in at tap 25 because we had coupons for a free burger / sandwich from our 50/50 tickets from an Oilers game.  We received our orders promptly And correctly. My short rib butter was very good. It is one I will return for!

I unfortunately can't comment on the food as I never got to actually eat anything but I can comment on the lack of organization/communication. We went to try and get a table at about 11:00 a.m. and we were told it would be about a 25 minute wait. I was surprised as the restaurant was only 3/4 full with lots of empty tables but I figured maybe they provide the room service to the hotel too or something. When they buzzed us to come back about a half hour later the hostess didn't appear to have any idea what was going on. They paged about 4 groups of people back at the same time so there was a lot of confusion. We were seated and I asked for a lunch menu as it was now 1145. After waiting for awhile I was told they weren't serving lunch until after the backlog of waiting customers were seated. What? How does that make any sense. The breakfast menu they gave us said breakfast could only be ordered until 1130. I was so annoyed/hangry by that point and not in the mood for breakfast that we just got up and left. The only reason I gave 2 stars was because our waitress was actually very nice and apologetic about the whole thing.  Overall, I was not impressed and definitely not interested in coming back.

This place is located inside the River Cree casino and can get quite busy.  We eat here quite often especially when they have a popular Wow entree of the month for $11.00 or the prime rib for $9.99 from Sunday to Thursday.  They offer a 10 oz. prime rib compared to a smaller size at competitor casinos.  It comes with an jus, horseradish, mashed potatoes, corn, carrots and beans and Yorkshire pudding.

There is also a Monday to Wednesday special on the menu featuring a few items for only $7.00.  That is such a good deal!  I've tried the Ranch chicken burger with fries and it sure fills me up.  If you aren't ordering a special, you can get 10 percent off your food by printing off the coupon from the kiosk in the casino.

I've enjoyed the beef dip as well as the Thai beef noodle bowl.  The Thai flavour was strong and spicy and came with chow mein noodles however I thought they were a little skimpy on the noodles so I mentioned it to our server.  Unfortunately I think it depends on who's working in the kitchen that day since he said sometimes you get more and sometimes less.

It's busy on hockey game nights as there are several tv's.  If you want to grab a bite before a concert, make sure to arrive early or you may not get a table.  When it's packed, it can get quite noisy.

I would give a higher rating as the food is always good but the service could be better.  The servers aren't really friendly and don't come by often enough.  When it's busy, it seems like they don't come back to offer drink refills or ask if everything is okay.

So next time you are at River Cree, give this place a try!
Great service here at the Cree at Tap 25. Good food and got it us very fast too! Had the chicken burger and Craig had the club. Oh yeah, and a cocktail or two as well.
Slow ass service not busy at all told them was going for smoke and was gone 15 minutes came back everything gone and put away order cancelled after telling them I was just having s smoke .

I attended a stag party that started here. And what a disaster. Even though a reservation was made because there was so many of us, they weren't ready when we showed up. So we pushed a bunch of tables together to seat as many of us as we could. They eventually moved us... and yet once again not enough tables. Nobody was really impressed with their meals - the ppl who ordered steak were the happiest - but I know my chicken was rubbery.
The service wasn't anything special. I do believe the waitress told us to get our 'manties' out of a knot. The managers give you a lot of talk but can't live up to it from the amount of mistakes they made.
No need to show up again.

For bar food it's actually pretty good. Have eaten here and even went out on a limb and tried the prime rib and surprisingly was really good. Meal was quick and hot and tasty. Plus there is a tv in every corner of the place to watch the highlights
yummy sirloin that will not hurt your wallet,perfect sides that goes with it ...service is fast,servers are quick and great,bottom line i will definitely comeback and recommend the restaurant.....

Tap 25 has the typical bar food.  They have specials for seniors, Monday-Wednesday $7 deals, and Sunday-Thursday $11 meal for those with the Player's Card.  You can get a 10% coupon when you swipe your card at the various machines in the casino.

I've been here numerous times including before a show at the Venue and would come at least 2 hours in advance as there could be a wait for a table.  Recently, they have been advertising their $3.99 breakfast special and is offered daily in April.  There are 10 specials to choose from: eggs Benedict, two eggs any style with meat, hashbrowns, and toast, made to order omelette, crepe omelette, Reuben, croissant BLT, waffles, quiche, french toast, pancakes, and English muffin sandwich.  Most come with hashbrowns or fruit cup.  Coffee, tea or juice is 99 cents, as is a side order of meat or fruit cup.  I ordered the made to order omelette with ham, green onion, and tomato. 

Although it wasn't a full house, it was busy for a Tuesday morning.  We sat with all the TVs around showing sports, and horse racing on bar chairs.  My chair was unbalanced but not bad enough to have to move and the table was small but we were able to fit our food and drink on it.

When my plate arrived, the hashbrowns were a little overcooked and browned.  I had to ask for jam for the toast and the waiter promptly brought it.  My omelette wasn't hot, just a little warm, and it tasted alright but too many onions for my liking.  

Service was friendly, price was good, and food ok (but not too greasy like a breakfast place I've been).
Good service horrible prices on beer but still good after a hockey game. Wings are fantastic.

This place was good before the menu got changed and the staff got replaced. Now it's a joke. Servers don't know anything about the menu or what's available on tap. Their poor attitude and complete disregard for guest experience makes me wonder how they're still in business. I've never felt so disregarded as a customer.

The new menu is very small and limited, with many dishes being available only at certain times of the day. Bring back the old menu, and re-hire the management & staff who understood that customers don't want to be treated as an unwelcome annoyance and I'll come back. Until then, forget it.

Please note, this review is for drinks only... we did not eat. Allow me to rant for a moment. We came here for a couple of beers before the Matt Good show at The Venue at River Cree. 25 taps, one would expect a bit of selection and choice. Nope, just another spot with all the draft taps controlled by Molson. No craft beers (and no, Granville Island while delicious is not craft... it's owned by Molson). I want to try something new and different when I hit a spot that advertises 25 taps in their business name, not be served Molsons mass brewed regulars and associated European beers. Canadian, Coors Light, Guinness, Strongbow... all the unoriginals are available here folks! Booooooo....

This is a cool spot inside the casino with a view of the ice rink. That's an interesting twist. Full bar with a good assortment of beers. When you need a break from the slot machines or are looking for a quick bite before a show this is a great option!

Really good Prime Rib dinner tonight.
Happy hour wine $4.75 a glass.
My dinner came out very quickly
Good selection on the menu
Nice atmosphere
Friendly staff
I will try something different tonight

Service is a little slow, but this is a cool spot inside the casino with a view of the ice rink. That's an interesting twist. Full bar with a good assortment of beers. The pizza specials are really good and the nachos are delish! When you need a break from the slot machines or are looking for a quick bite before a show this is a great opportunity.

I stopped in at Tap 25 last night before my boyfriends hockey game. He was playing on the South Rink, so I requested a table that looks out at the rink - not a problem at all!! I was seated within a couple of minutes and only waited a few more before the waitress asked what I wanted to drink. I ordered the 10 oz. Prime Rib special for $9.99, which came with fries (I substituted with Sweet Potato Fries for an additional $1.00), veggies, and Yorkshire pudding. I did find that my prime rib was a little tough, especially for Medium Rare, but it was delicious regardless. 
My waitress for the evening, Myranda, was very polite and knowledgeable about the menu. I have been here a few times in the past and the sandwiches and burgers are good as well. Very quick service, delicious food, and affordable prices. I will always be a repeat customer.

The mornings at Tap 25, as you can expect, are fairly low key. My wife and I went there for a midmorning snack last week. The waiter was super-polite and quick to respond to our questions and musings. I ordered the English Muffin Sandwich with a fruit cup on the side. The sandwich was warm, meaty, and toasty. Imagine how great a McDonalds Egg McMuffin® would be if it was real food . . . well that's what my English Muffin Sandwich at Tap 25 was like. The waiter was quick to replenish my coffee and frequently checked back to make sure we had all we needed.

Tonight we showed up for supper. Not surprisingly it was much more crowded and noisy at this time of the day. I ordered the Top Sirloin Steak with gravy on the side. The steak was very good - juicy and tender. They accidentally brought me a double order of gravy. Then again, Freud said there are no accidents when it comes to gravy (or something to that effect). We ordered wings as an appetizer. The wings are surprisingly meaty and hearty. Most places serve up wings that taste like they come from a frozen food section at any old grocery store - dry and dainty. The hot wings aren't as hot as I would have liked, but that's personal preference. I'm a connoisseur of all things hot.

With all the TV screens beaming every sporting event and horserace going on in the world it gets a little nerve-wracking. But what can you expect - it's a casino. Our waitress was suffering from the same case of sensory overload that I was. Her manners were a little bit lacking as was her sense of urgency. She wasn't rude - just a little stone-faced. I like to be polite and say 'thanks' when I'm being served. There was no 'you're welcome' or 'no problem' or anything of the like. She just dropped the food in front me and moved on to her next tasking. I guess Tap 25 don't program their night time servers to be civil. She noticed that my Coke was low and asked if I wanted a refill. I said that I did and she was gone for about 15 minutes. I thought she must have been brewing a fresh batch in a vat in the kitchen and maybe had to fly to Peru to get some coca leaves.

So I'll gladly return to Tap 25 for breakfast but I won't be in a hurry to return here for supper.

Only reason this is a 2 star is because the service was very good for a busy night. The food on the other hand was abysmal to say the least. I ordered the bacon burger and had to send that back, the beef tasted way off (I never send food back) the waitress was kind enough to take it back and bring me the meat lovers pizza (my fault for ordering another item with beef) and that was also terrible. I don't like to make a fuss so I paid and went on my way. Come here for drinks, not food.

If you are expecting a lot for the 11.99 prime rib deal  don't get your hopes up. All the food was BLAND. Cut of meat was big enough but tasteless. Yorkshire pudding was cold tough and rubbery. Not on my recommended list.

My first impression every time I walk in the door is yuck!!!! One day someone will remove that awful air freshener for good. Quite frankly, it smells like something more suitable for a public restroom. Nice rooms, comfy beds, great views, clean, friendly staff, that's why we keep coming back. We ate at  the Seafood Buffet while there, okay for the price, Great coffee :) I wish the gift store would carry handmade native items made by local artisans from Enoch.

I was unfortunately so disappointed with this hotel.  Their website (albeit rather unprofessional) touts this hotel and casino as being a 4.5 star resort.  It is rayed on various sites as being a 4 star hotel.  I have to say, I was at a 3 star radisson that was significantly nicer than this hotel.  

I disliked almost every aspect of my stay.   The restaurants were disappointing, to say the least.  The smokey smell from the casino gave me and my party headaches and it drifted into the hotel and the rooms. 

Although they do not charge the price of a 4 star, they should absolutely not tout that they are.  It leads with himgh expectations only to be disappointed. 

The positives about this property are that it is clean and the beds are comfortable.

Unfortunately, I left smelling like an ash tray.

This hotel has impressed me from check in to check out.  Great customer service from top to bottom.  Clean..all the amenities needed and great restaurants available.  Shuttle bus available to west edmonton mall.  I will definitely stay again

Nice stay at the river cree. staff is so friendly! Exceptional kudos to the staff at check in and servers at the buffet. The hotel is well maintained. Rooms comfortable. The wifi was free with a marriot members card and an accidental pay per view purchase was removed bill without hesitation. Touchy remote so those with children beware. who wouldnt be upset to pay 17 bucks for a mark paul gosselaar flick. Ha. Casino paid me out a couple thousand.  good cocktail deals at the centre bar. This casino is smoking in some areas and you can bring your cocktail to the machines.  Like any hotel of a particular size there is a lot of walking involved. The hallways seem endless ha. BTW best hot tub I've ever came across in a hotel. Hot and deep. You'll love it

This hotel is overrated and certainly not worth the money for the amenities provided. I booked this hotel through priceline and looking at the word "resort" in the name I felt there would be some really good amenities, but when I arrived I was very disppointed. It just turned out to be an overrated motel. In addition for the night I stayed their pool was not working. For the amenities provided I could have stayed at a cheaper place. Only good thing is room service was good and that is the reason I am giving 2 stars. This was he first time I stayed in a Marriott and disappointed, but still hopeful that other Marriott's will not be like this one.

I'd like to echo Nandan's review in support of this Marriott property. I spent in excess of 75 days a year in hotels and I was fortunate enough to enjoy a nights stay at this location. The room upgrade was granted on request, a personal greeting from the front desk with a written note in my room was a welcome touch. The service here is intuitive without being intrusive - not an easy feat.

Very nice accommodations with easy access to the River Creek casino if that's your thing. Excellent overall experience!

This Marriott is connected to the River Cree and great for those who are gamblers. The parking lot is very large and it's free parking. There are three elevators and there was never a lineup and actually nobody in the elevator while we were in it.

The room was comfortable with two double beds, a desk, A mini fridge and a coffee maker. The coffee maker is underneath the TV and so it is kind of low and not visible behind the door. They do provide a couple of tea bags, coffee, sugar, and whiteners. There's ample counter space by the bathroom sink and great shower head in the tub.

On the second floor there is a large gym with lots of equipment and it was always empty when I was around there. There is a man's and a woman's washroom in the gym and it's also connected by a door to the hot tub and the pool. The hot tub has a capacity of five people and both time we went to use it there was nobody there but a few more people joined in after. The whole pool is the same depth. There's also a shower but it takes a while for the water to warm up. On the far end of the pool there are towels and there are lounge chairs around. Just outside of the gym and pool area there's another door where you will find a large washer and dryer. It's free to use and there's a machine if you require soap.

There is a Starbucks just off of the lobby in the hotel. We went here at 7 AM in the morning and there was a line of people waiting to get their coffee. They don't except Starbucks gift cards though as they are not an official Starbucks store. There's also the Kitchen Bistro restaurant which offers a breakfast buffet. Inside the casino there is also Tap25 which offers a cheaper breakfast however it is not served in till 9:30 AM. Dinners options include the buffet (although expect to wait hours on Monday or Wednesday due to 2 for 1 coupons that Player's card holders have), Sage, or Tap25 inside the casino. 

There is free Wi-Fi that you can connect to however they ask if you want to upgrade for a charge so be careful which option you're choosing.

This is a great hotel in West Edmonton but not ideal if you do not have a vehicle. Costco is close by but there are not too many restaurants around if you don't have a car. I had a good sleep even though there was some noise coming from the hallway after 11 PM but throughout the night it was quiet. Or for those that don't want to sleep or can't sleep you can always head downstairs and play in the casino.

I've booked banquets here a couple of times, and have attended banquets here. From an organizing perspective, the banquet staff have always been very helpful, and we've never had any issues with our event. The hotel lobby is beautifully decorated with lots of sitting area, and there's always a very friendly doorman.  I am always satisfied with the food as well, as are the guests, and the banquet prices were very competitive. The only reason I haven't booked recently is that we prefer another location more central in the city. But if you're up for driving a little bit, I definitely recommend he River Cree banquet services. It's also great because after the banquet, people can go have fun in the Casino if they so choose.

Location: 
The hotel is located in the quiet Enoch neighbourhood and is relatively close to the West Edmonton Mall. It's not a happenning area but its actually nice, quiet and I enjoyed seeing the the sun rise on the horizon every morning. If you want to go out, be prepared to drive as even food may be hard a find nearby. The hotel has a casino as well which is a huge crowd puller. I believe the hotel is halfway between the airport and downtown in terms of distance. 


Front Desk: 
Fantastic staff and all requests made during my reservation were met. They gave me an upgrade and the staff met my expectations of being at a Marriott. 

Parking: 
There is tons of outdoor parking available. Valet service is available in the evenings/nights at the Casino entrance. The only issue I had was there is no power outlet to plug in your car and I'd be concerned during the cold weather. 

Room: 
The room was clean and were pretty new and since I got an upgrade, I don't really have anything to complain about. They provided enough towels and the beds were one of the most comfortable I have ever had. Housekeeping and room service staff were amazing. If you are an elite member, you have access to the concierge lounge as well. This is one of the rare hotels where the lounge is open on weekends as well. The internet is $16 per day unless its part of your rate. Laundry facilities are available on the 2nd floor. 

Restaurant:
They have 3 restaurants. The Kitchen -  a la carte and buffet. They  have buffet theme nights as well that serves seafood, asian cuisine etc. Tap 25 which is a sports bar which is great for catching a game. Sage - fine dining. I only ate at the sports bar and the kitchen a couple of times and had a good time. Nothing to rave about but nothing to complain about either. Room service from the other restaurant was worth it as well. There is a starbucks coffee for your caffiene doses.  

Healthclub/gym: 
They have a decent sized gym although I'd expect and appreciate a bit more equipment than free weights, treadmills and bikes. They have a pool and an ice rink as well. 

Overall:
I had a very pleasant stay overall. I hardly ran into the casino crowd but that is more prone to happen on weekends. I rather not give it a 5 star rating but based on most hotels like Hiltons, Delta's and Crowns in most Canadian cities, this could be there. Let's say that overall its a 4 star experience.

I recently saw Joe Rogan at The Venue (located at the River Cree Casino).  Joe Rogan was hilarious!  I honestly wasn't expecting much but he definitely put on a great show.  The Venue is like a "military tent" according to Joe.  It was very warm inside considering it was a huge tent and it was surprisingly comfortable.  The chairs were great and the rows had enough leg room that you weren't squirming and fidgeting the whole show.  There were two bars located at the entrance of The Venue (the back of the tent) which got extremely busy at times.  There were numerous bartenders at each bar though so the lines moved at a pretty good pace.  I had a great experience at The Venue and I had a great time with Joe Rogan - I will be buying tickets for his next show in Edmonton!

It is newly "renovated" and it is better than it was. You no longer need to go outside to get into The Venue which is a bonus in the winter. I don't enjoy that there is only one level seating. If you are in the back rows just hope you're tall enough to see. It still seems a bit temporary in the sense that you have to leave The Venue to use the restrooms. However there is one just outside the doors so the trek is not the worst. I like the progress. I can't wait to go back when it is fully completed.

The Venue has changed but is still only accessible through the River Cree casino.  The line to get in is more efficient and less crowded.  Washrooms have been added and the seats have improved, more room and more comfortable.

Popular performers continue to come here at good ticket prices.  The two screens beside the stage are good for people who don't sit that close.

They should make room for a dancing area for people to groove with the music which would make the experience more fun.  Some concerts say no pictures or video but no one reinforces this.

This place is still good for a night out as you are not paying high prices, can park for free and try your luck in the casino before or after your show!  Maybe your ticket and drinks can be free?

I wrote a long, rambly review over at the River Cree's Yelp page (http://www.yelp.ca/biz/river-cree-resort-and-casino-enoch?hrid=HgeD464reIG8a51xYtWyKg) before I realised The Venue had it's own page.

I won't bother reiterating everything again here, so here is a quick list of pros & cons:

Pros:
1. It attracts great artists.
2. Free parking.
3. Decent sound system.
4. Very friendly staff

Cons:
1. Have to enter through the casino, then walk down a long hallway and OUTSIDE to get to the venue (ps.  Coat check is inside the casino, not the venue.  So if you use the coat check, just pray there isn't a line up outside the venue in the winter!
2. Drink prices are attrocious ($9.00 each for a standard sized highball)
3. Folding chairs that are strapped together and pushed flush up against each other (you are guaranteed to be touching the person next to you)
4.  Restrooms are located back in the hockey rink area, so you have to go back outside to get there.
5. ONLY ONE EXIT FOR 2100 PEOPLE!
6.  All seating is on the same level, so if you're too far towards the back, you probably don't see much.
 

I'll be back because that's where the great comedy shows are.  But I hope Jeff is right about the new venue going up on the west end in 2017!

Over the years I have attended a number of (pre) 80s flashback shows (Rick Springfield, Air Supply, Beach Boys, Cheech and Chong, and The Spazmatics 80s cover band) at The Venue.  It is a large white tent just outside of River Cree resort.  If it's cold out, you will feel it as you have to walk from inside the casino to the tent.

For concerts, they will set up the venue with rows of chairs in 3 sections.  For concerts, I like to sit in the middle section.  However, the chairs are stuck together with cable ties and they are so close together you could be rubbing legs with strangers on both sides.  The chairs aren't so comfortable if you have to sit there longer than a few hours so good idea to get up for a drink or use the washroom in the casino.  Other events, they will sometimes set it up with tables and 8 chairs around while leaving the dance floor empty.  This is great as there's lots of room for dancing and it's not too crowded.

The sound quality is not bad for an outside tent venue.  Not the most comfortable setting for a concert or show but ok for a casino venue.  If you are going to catch a show and want to do dinner before, I recommend you are there at least 2 hours before the show to ensure you get a table and have time to eat.  You can also get your hand stamped early to avoid the line ups close to show time.

They get good acts to perform here so it can be a good time still but the venue is absolute garbage. Every performer I've seen here makes the joke that they are in an aircraft hanger. The casino figures people will pay anyways so why bother with giving them a good experience. I find a lot of time I watch the performers on the video screen not because I want to but because the setup draws me to them. Oh and they charge 9 bucks for a beer. Ridiculous.

Cutting to the chase, I've been here three times for concerts. Rick Springfield a couple of years ago, Huey Lewis and the News last August and most recently Steve Earle and the Dukes. I really like this place as a music venue. The sound is always good and getting in and out of the River Cree is a whole lot easier than Rogers Place or the Coliseum.
The only thing I dislike is the fact that you have to purchase beverage tickets to get a drink. It just seems like another line that one has to endure just to grab a beer. I have loathed this every time I experience it. This made me not purchase a drink on this night.

Other than that, "The Venue" is a very nice room to see a band in. Big enough to attract some decent names, yet small enough to make it intimate.

So, yes this venue has some pretty awesome concerts/performances/shows. Much like a Vegas casino, this place tries to book some big name performances for this place out on the Enoch Cree Nation. And the venue itself is clean and large. It feels a bit like a barn (and the performer we came to see remarked on this fact). We came exceedingly early on for our show because the doors were at 7pm and the show was at 9pm and prior to this show I had never visited this place. And frankly, I wouldn't seek this place out in the future, unless the show was as good as this one was -- it was a really good show! They provided free earplugs (which was very helpful, especially as we had EXCELLENT seats), and we made it through security without any lines. The Casino in the early evening only smelled mildly of cigarette smoke (yes the Casino has smoking as it is on the reserve land -- more on this later). 

We noticed that the washrooms were VERY poorly labeled. It felt like there was a constant stream of men mistakenly walking halfway into the women's restroom because of this labeling issue. The signage could be very much improved. The seats themselves in the venue are comfortable and the show itself was great.

The fact that the entrance to the venue is through the casino is likely a good business decision for the casino but for someone like myself who literally cannot breathe properly when exposed to the amount of secondhand smoke that was present as we left the show this is definitely a downside. I HATED walking through the crowds to get to clean air. If I had been attending the show on my own, I'm entirely unsure how capable I would have been of getting out of there safely. I know that the venue has good security and lots of first aid staff on site (I saw them), but this was horrible.

Getting out of the parking lot after the show was also a nightmare. It took us around 25 minutes to leave the parking lot to get out. After that the drive home was okay. I understand that there is shuttle service from West Edmonton Mall, that this venue is well served by taxi cabs, and that transit sort of gets here as well, but it's not terribly accessible by most estimations. At least there is a hotel here.

The Venue looks more like an aircraft hangar or an army field kitchen than a concert hall. The sound is half-decent though but it could be a lot better. The last two concerts I saw here, the sound kept cutting in and out of one of the PA systems which was totally annoying. It reminded me of the time I had a bad speaker in my car which cut in and out whenever I hit a bump.

The security and usher staff at The Venue are always friendly and jovial. The barcode scanners that they use to scan tickets at the door never work properly and they always have a clever one-liner to spout off about how unreliable modern technology is.

The absolute worst thing about this place is the seating. The Venue's seating plan consists of around two thousand metal folding chairs all zip-tied together. It's bad enough that the chairs are cheap and uncomfortable but zap-strapping them together just makes it ten times worse because they're simply too close together. It looks like a concert hall that caters to anorexics and bulimics only - and I'm a skinny guy, so that's saying a lot. Prepare to spend an intimate evening with your neighbour rubbing your thighs and elbows together. I understand that the Venue probably does this to keep the chairs organized in their rows and to keep people from tossing them in the air when their ass gets too sore to sit any longer but there has to be a better way to secure the chairs than this. When purchasing tickets I always try to get a seat at the end of the aisle so I at least have breathing room on one side of me. The seats aren't numbered either which makes it even more fun to find your chair if you're seated in the middle of the row. You'll have to count your way in.

There's only two sets of small doors to get in and out of the Venue, both located at the back of the structure. These doors lead to a sharp ninety-degree turn into an incredibly narrow hallway which brings you back into the casino. If there's ever a fire in this concert hall it is going to be an absolute nightmare to get out of there. Imagine two thousand people rushing for those two small doors and that small hallway at the same time? I hope The Venue has better plan for fire evacuation than they do for seating. Great White are playing here in a couple of months so I guess I'll find out then. (Was that tasteless?)

Other than the seats, the Venue is actually quite spacious to move around in. Lots of room between the back rows to get to the beer line and the merchandise counter. I think the building needs a separate entrance and exit but being that it's part of a casino, that will never happen. How will they get people to gamble if they don't have to move through the casino to get to the concert?

We came here to see the American Filipino comedian JoKoy. He has a couple of Netflix specials. He's extremely funny and very popular. I immediately bought tickets for my family when I found out he would be performing here. In fact, this show was sold out 6 months ago!!

This was my first time to come to The Venue. I thought it looked spacious. The lighting and the awesome music got me pumped! The atmosphere was very club like.

I was glad to see that there were washrooms close by. There was no need to go out into the casino and to re-enter. I was also grateful that there were quite a number of stalls available. When there is booze at a venue, it is very convenient to have nearby washrooms.

We had assigned seating. Large free standing signs indicated the sections (eg. Section B). Our rows and sections were also indicated by signs on the floors (under the chairs along the aisles) and seat numbers on the chairs.

During the show, JoKoy was joking about how the The Venue looked more like a tent, instead of a theatre. I have to admit the white interior looked plastic and tent like. But overall, I feel that the venue adequately served its purpose.

I appreciated the giant screens that advertised upcoming events. I was also glad for the opportunity to have a close up view of JoKoy, because of these large screens.

The main floor seats were all on the same level. It would've been nice if the seats were on an incline or if there were risers, to allow for a better view of the stage. There was an upper level viewing lounge at the back. Those seats had tables. 

I would definitely consider coming back here again. The quality of the talent that comes to perform here are impressive. A definite draw. For me, I had a good time for my first experience here!

I feel sort of bad giving The Venue 2 stars, but there's a few things counting against that lead me to drop from 3.

The room really is an aircraft hangar, there's no other way to describe it. I was thinking, what if they were to put some sort of cool lighting installation in spanning the length of the hall? Sort of like what Glasgow has in Royal Exchange Square :) 

Seating is basically bench style, not a great move considering that if you have a giant sitting in from of you (I did) this limits your view to essentially nill. 

On the plus side, sound was good - which is obviously important for a live music venue. Incidentally I was at the Tea Party show. 

I will be going back - Bryan Ferry in August, however it's definitely not my favourite room for live music.

In my original review of The Venue I called them out on their lack of accessibility getting in and out of the place. There were only two narrow doors located at the rear of the tent (yes, it's a tent) to herd people in and out. These doors led to a tiny hallway which took you back into the casino.

Oddly enough, a few weeks after I wrote that review River Cree "voluntarily" closed this facility due to its not meeting safety codes.

They have now put up a new temporary entertainment venue set up which is just another white tent that looks a lot like the old one. The difference is that this one has several emergency exits on either side and there is substantially more room to move at the main entrance/exit at the back (those two narrow doors I spoke of). Why it took them seven months to decide to just put up another tent is beyond me but that's what they did.

They still have metal folding chairs tied together for their seating arrangements. So if you weigh more than 120 pounds you're going to be uncomfortable sitting in there.

Everything about River Cree's concert venue just screams out "cheap, cheap, cheap." And by cheap, I don't mean affordable. River Cree's concert productions are a gaudy, transparent attempt to pack you in and get your money. Both of their concert halls have been lame-ass tents filled with the cheapest chairs money can buy and crammed literally as close together as they can get them. I would be embarrassed to stage concerts at this place with such quality venues as the Northern Jubilee Auditorium and The Winspear Centre in the city.

For most of River Cree's concerts you can also purchase what they call a Fanatics Package for $100 which consists of a front row seat and a rushed photo op. No autographs are allowed. They always claim that it is the band that refuses to sign them but that's BS because I've caught up with a few performers after their show here and they're always happy to sign their merch for you. Lou Gramm, Queensrÿche, and members Grand Funk Railroad to name a few. I suspect that River Cree don't allow autographs during these Fanatic events because there's no money in it for them. I tweeted Queensrÿche about this issue and they said it was the venue/promoter who made that rule and that they would take care of me if I saw them after the concert. At the back entrance to the casino there are several posters on display autographed by performers who have played at The Venue over the years so obviously River Cree have no issues with being autograph hounds themselves.

In order to get your photo you have to return to the casino at a later date and pick it up at the Players Club desk. Here's what they DON'T tell you in their literature--the photo is a mere 5x7 with NO digital version available. This is just further case-in-point to the fact that River Cree are living in a different century. Everything is about bringing you back into the casino to spend money. If they had any marketing sense they would include a digital version of the photo with the "Fanatics Package" and encourage people to share it on social media with a promotional hash tag to maximize their exposure as a happening music venue. 

They also oversell on how "professional" the photo is. During the Queensrÿche photo op the band weren't even centred on the backdrop. The drummer spoke up and pointed out that we all had to move down to the left because the guitarist was being pushed up against the wall. The photographer just ignored him and kept snapping away. The drummer just gave up and griped that he wasn't even listening to him. So in addition to being blind, the photographer is also deaf. (It's the same photographer every time, btw.)

The casino is currently constructing a new entertainment facility out back behind their hockey rink. This one is an actual hard structure and not a tent. River Cree are promising two levels of seating and comfy chairs for this one. Rumour has it that there's going to be a new 4,100-person venue for live music, comedy, trade shows, and sporting events opening in west Edmonton in 2017 which could be serious competition for River Cree so the casino is probably upping their game for this reason. They should also update their Fanatics Packages to be more competitive with similar products being offered in this century.

I'll be back with my third review of The Venue when it opens in a few months.

We were at Billy Idol last night. And the sound was so terrible we had to leave early. The bass was so loud that when I sat down, I could feel the vibration in my chest. Even my phone was vibrating in my hands.

At one point, the speakers blew and started that high pitch ringing noise. This hurt my ear so much I started feeling nausea.

Now, let me start off by saying that I am a musician. I have 40 years of experience and started performing at 6 years old in my first recital. I've been to the majority of venues in town and even performed at the Festival Place.

This was SO disappointing. I don't know if the venue was at fault, or the band. Billy Idol was disappointing as well. He was terribly out of shape and out of breath by the third song. I thought he was going to collapse on stage. Anyone who gave him a high rating for that performance - has no clue. It was awful. I'm pretty sure he missed some lyrics and he let the band do most of the work. The band however, was top notch. Steve Stevens was the selling point for me and made the trip worth it.

For $133.25 per ticket, I expected better. Ticket prices are ridiculous. And not worth it for this venue.

The highlight of the night was Steve Stevens. And literally, running into the band as they were rushing into the venue. They were late and obviously missed soundcheck.

The resort itself is fine for all kinds of functions. But the venue needs work. I've been to a lot of rock concerts. U2. Bon Jovi. Alanis. Even Twisted Sister - and none were as terrible as the show was last night. I wanted to love it. But as a previous performer, I just couldn't.

I've never walked out early out of a concert. But the combination of being surrounded by drunk people and the busted speakers, we just couldn't deal. My ears are still ringing today.
